summary: Master Advanced HR Analytics for effective strategic decision-making. Enroll in our training course and gain the insights needed to lead your HR initiatives.
lede: Advanced HR analytics helps HR professionals turn workforce data into evidence for strategic decisions. Designed for practitioners who interpret metrics, advise leaders or build reports, the course covers KPI scorecards, workforce trend analysis, headcount and turnover forecasting, and HR program ROI evaluation. Hands-on work in Excel and Power BI includes dashboard design and executive storytelling, with attention to data quality, privacy, fairness and bias.
audienceIntro: This course is tailored for HR professionals who already work with HR data and need to strengthen their advanced HR analytics capability to support strategic decision making. You should be directly involved in interpreting workforce metrics, advising leadership, or building dashboards and reports that influence people decisions. This course is designed for: HR Analytics Manager responsible for building workforce dashboards and models. People Analytics Lead designing KPI frameworks and decision-support insights. Senior HR Business Partner advising leaders using data-driven workforce analysis. HR Director or Head of HR aligning people analytics with business strategy. Talent Management Specialist optimizing succession and high-potential analytics. Recruitment Analytics Specialist tracking sourcing funnels and hiring performance. Compensation and Benefits Analyst evaluating pay, rewards, and retention metrics. Learning and Development Analytics Specialist measuring training impact and ROI. Workforce Planning Analyst modeling headcount scenarios and capacity risks. HRIS Manager integrating data from HR systems for analytics and reporting.
modules: Predictive HR Analytics and Workforce Forecasting
HR Program Impact Measurement and ROI
HR Analytics Dashboards and Data Visualization
Talent Analytics for Strategic Workforce Decisions
Strategic Storytelling and HR Analytics Communication
Integrating HR Analytics into Strategy and Operations
prerequisites: You should bring a laptop capable of running Microsoft Excel and, where possible, a BI tool such as Power BI or Tableau. Access to sample or anonymized HR datasets (e.g., exports from your HRIS or ATS) will allow you to apply concepts directly to your context, though the course will also provide practice data. Prior exposure to HR reporting, metrics, and basic analytics is required, but you do not need programming skills or advanced statistics; analytical techniques are taught with a focus on practical HR application.
